blocks.text: 1. What are Embeddings?

blocks.alt: A word goes through an embedding to become a vector of numbers

blocks.text: What are Embeddings opens the Embeddings module by defining the core representation retrieval depends on, shifting focus from splitting text to representing it.
It converts a chunk of text into a list of numbers that captures its meaning.
2. Chunking Recap
The entire Chunking module, closed out in Chunk Size Optimization, produced well sized, well bounded chunks ready for the next step.
Embeddings take those finished chunks and turn them into searchable vectors.

blocks.text: 3. From Words To Numbers
As with retrieval using embeddings in What Is RAG, a computer cannot directly compare meaning between two pieces of text.
Converting text into numbers gives meaning something that can actually be measured.
4. What A Vector Actually Is

blocks.alt: A vector is an ordered list of numbers

blocks.text: A vector is just an ordered list of numbers, like coordinates in space.
An embedding is one specific kind of vector, produced by a trained model.
5. Similar Meaning Means Nearby Points

blocks.alt: Similar words end up as nearby points in space

blocks.text: Two chunks with similar meaning produce embeddings that land close together in that vector space.
Two unrelated chunks, by contrast, land far apart.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: The sentences "a dog is running" and "a puppy is sprinting" produce embeddings that land close together in vector space, even though they share almost no exact words, because their underlying meaning is similar.

blocks.text: 6. How A Model Learns This Mapping

blocks.alt: Training data goes through a model to produce a learned mapping

blocks.text: As with self supervised learning in Deep Learning Fundamentals, an embedding model trains on huge amounts of text to learn this mapping.
No one hand writes the rules for which words are similar.
7. Embeddings Are Fixed Length

blocks.alt: A short text and a long text both produce the same length vector

blocks.text: Every embedding from a given model has the exact same number of dimensions.
A short sentence and a long paragraph both produce vectors of identical length.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: A common misconception is that longer text produces a longer embedding vector. The vector length depends only on the model used, never on how much text was fed into it.

blocks.text: 8. Embeddings As The Entry Point To Retrieval

blocks.alt: Text goes through embedding into vector search

blocks.text: Every chunk produced by the Chunking module gets converted into one of these vectors.
Those vectors become the searchable representation stored in a vector database, the subject of a later module.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why Embeddings Are Essential To RAG

blocks.alt: Needing to compare meaning, not just text, points toward using embeddings

blocks.text: Any system that needs to compare meaning rather than exact text needs embeddings.
Exact keyword matching can work without embeddings, but it misses paraphrased or related content.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming embedding vector length depends on the input text's length rather than the model used.
Comparing embeddings from two different models as if they shared the same vector space.
Treating embeddings as an exact keyword match rather than a measure of semantic similarity.
Forgetting that embeddings are learned from data, not manually defined rules.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Embeddings convert a chunk of text into a fixed length list of numbers capturing its meaning.
Computers cannot directly compare meaning between text; embeddings make meaning measurable.
A vector is an ordered list of numbers; an embedding is one produced by a trained model.
Chunks with similar meaning produce embeddings that land close together in vector space.
Embedding models learn this mapping from huge amounts of training text, not hand written rules.
Every embedding from a given model has the same fixed number of dimensions regardless of input length.
Embeddings are the entry point that turns chunks into searchable vectors for a vector database.
Systems needing to compare meaning, not just exact keywords, require embeddings.
